properties.Narratives: Destruction of Al-Faluja Cemetery
properties.Description: Satellite imagery released by the New York Times on December 10, 2023, revealed that Israeli military operations have led to the partial destruction of around six cemeteries in northern Gaza, including Al-Falujah Cemetery, since the beginning of their ground offensive. The images showed evidence of recent activity and possible military vehicle presence, with photos depicting the destruction of graveyards. This event sparked mourning among people, as the Israeli aggression did not spare their deceased ones.
properties.Quote_1: "Destruction of my father's and my wife's family's graves in Al-Faluja Cemetery in Jabalia Camp.. Our solace is that the souls are in the safety of their Creator." - Moutasem
properties.quotes: "Destruction of my father's and my wife's family's graves in Al-Faluja Cemetery in Jabalia Camp.. Our solace is that the souls are in the safety of their Creator." - Moutasem SOURCE

properties.Narratives: Disruption of Prayers at Al-Omari Mosque
properties.Description: The Great Omari Mosque is the oldest mosque in Palestine that has been built, destroyed, rebuilt, and repurposed between a mosque and a church several times. During the rule of Salah al-din, he converted it to a mosque one last time, and it remained as such during the Mamluk and Ottoman periods. Now, as a Muslim institution for almost 900 years, it is one of the most important places for worship in Gaza. Quotes and anecdotes by the people of Gaza show the strong connection of the mosque to their collective memory.
properties.Quote_1: The first time I bought a camera in my life, I think it was around the year 2002. I went to photograph the Omari Mosque and its picturesque surroundings, reaching Saint Porphyrius Church and Katib Wilayat Mosque, that heart torn apart by Israel day after day. I still claim that I have the best photos taken of this area. But what is the use of photos? - Arafat Al-Haj
properties.Quote_2: "My favorite place in Gaza is the Great Omari Mosque. I like to pray and read the Quran there. The tall minaret is very unique" - Samira Elbaz, 9 years
properties.Quote_3: "My strongest memory is when as the director of Iwan (Center for Architectural Heritage), I was able to climb up the minaret. Looking down at the city was wonderful.  Being in the midst of heritage buildings imparts a sense of the history of the city in which one lives." – Dr. Suheir Ammar, Assistant Professor at the Islamic University of Gaza
properties.Quote_4: “My apartment was just next to the mosque, and we used to enjoy the pray of the early morning. My father’s shop is on the same road, same side of our apartment. So usually I would go to see my father, sometimes I used to work with my father till 65 [year 1965]. There was a door near AL-Qasriyah, I used to go with the stairs down until the end. You can go walking just to see, it’s a huge mosque – huge! You are taking about - the tall [height] of the mosque is maybe around 200 m or more even – more, and wider and beautiful!” – Avedis Djeghalian, Dentist and son of a photographer
properties.Quote_5: “When I was a child, I used to go with my grandmother to the mosque. She used to go every Friday […]. She would meet with other old women, chat, and listen to the Khutba, and pray. Then we would go back to her house, which wasn’t in the area, but she made that effort to like go that specific mosque. She lived there opposed to the mosque for a period of her life. So she has her own history in the area. So I just remember it as a place that connects me with my grandmother.” - Rawan Yaghi, Journalist
properties.Quote_6: When I was a child, I remember when my grandfather used to take me to the Omari Mosque to pray Dhuhr or Asr, and I was a little boy with him. I remember there were things we have lost today, which I may have seen in some mosques in Egypt and Istanbul. The religious rituals had a certain pattern: they would sit and recite the Quran, then the call to prayer, then they would go back to reciting the Quran and doing Tasbih, then the sermon would start, then they would pray, and afterward, they would do Tasbih again. - Ayman Abu Shaban, Architect at Gaza Municipality
properties.Quote_7: In this courtyard behind the worshippers, under the arches, there is a slightly elevated platform from the courtyard. I have sat there dozens of times for hours. The neighborhood children played football in the courtyard, the worshippers, the wholesale traders, the vendors, the porters, and the patrons of the Al-Zawiya Market. There is not a single person in Gaza for whom this courtyard does not represent a part of their connection to Gaza and its history. - Arafat Al-Haj
properties.Quote_8: The Omari Mosque is the memory of Gaza City and a symbol of its ability to renew and rise. Its state is inseparable from that of Gaza: its destruction reflects Gaza's destruction, and its reconstruction reflects Gaza's reconstruction. By praying in the Omari Mosque, Gazans affirm their commitment to life and their rejection of annihilation and extinction.

properties.Narratives: Disruption of Reading Activities Gaza's Municipality Library
properties.Description: A statement by the local government on November 27, 2023, stated that the occupation forces targeted the public library building, turning it into rubble. The strikes destroyed thousands of books, titles, documents, and the library’s halls and facilities. According to data mapped by the Beirut Urban Lab until May 3,2024, Israel targeted 68% of libraries in Gaza.
properties.Quote_1: So many memories and eternal friendships I experienced in the Gaza Public Library! - Abdul Rahman
properties.Quote_2: “I was a passionate reader, deeply in love with what is called a book. The book is incredibly precious… I used to come here to the library frequently, borrowing and reading books. I used to spend most of my times here, reading and spending my time between the books and their scents. After the place was destroyed by the occupation, there are no more books, no more library, and no place to read in. The place where we used to find comfort in is no more there. The place we developed our dreams, ambitions, and life goals is gone… The occupation destroyed all our libraries, our dreams, our schools, and our ambitions.” – Dania, a frequent library visitor
properties.media: Agence France-Presse (AFP) (November 29,2023)

properties.Narratives: Disruption of Education at Al-Azhar University
properties.Description: Repeated Israeli airstrikes in October and November 2023 targeted the main headquarters of Al-Azhar University in Gaza City and its branch in the area of Al-Mughraqa, stated the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor. An Israeli soldier stood in front of the destroyed university and mockingly exclaimed:  "To those who say why there is no education in Gaza. We bombed them. This is very bad. That way you will never be an engineer anymore." According to data mapped by the Beirut Urban Lab until May 3,2024, 71% of Gaza's universities have been targeted, and 7 of them are completely destroyed.

properties.Narratives: Shattered Lives in Rimal Neighborhood
properties.Description: The Rimal neighborhood, which was once the vibrant core of the Gaza Strip, has been almost completely destroyed in four days of heavy Israeli bombardment on the besieged territory. Israeli airstrikes have demolished the walls of apartment buildings, felled trees along the sidewalks, torn up streets bustling with businessmen and food vendors, and flattened university buildings, mosques, and offices ranging from Gaza’s main telecommunications company to international media outlets. Footage shows the massive destruction in Al Rimal Neighborhood.
properties.Quote_1: “That is the space of our public life, our community.” - A Palestinian businessman Ali al-Hiyak from his home near Rimal.
properties.CheckFootageSource: See footage from 00:00 to 00:21 here.

properties.Narratives: Gaza's Cultural Center Lost in the War
properties.Description: Situated in Gaza City's Al-Rimal neighborhood and established in 1985, the center was named after Palestinian businessman Rashad al-Shawa, a former mayor of Gaza. Designed by Syrian architect Saad Mohafell, the three-story building featured a library, spacious lounges for cultural events, and the Great Theater. During times of conflict, it provided refuge for many Palestinians. However, the center was ultimately destroyed in an Israeli airstrike, leaving it in ruins. Its director mourned the theater's loss, recognizing it as a place that depicted Gaza's hardships and showcased its beauty and resilience.

properties.Narratives: Disruption of Social Activities at Al-Saqqa Ancient House
properties.Description: On November 9, 2023, Al-Saqqa house, a 400-year-old- monument in Al-Shuja'ia neighborhood, was targeted by the Israeli forces along with many other historical, cultural, and archeological sites. Constructed in the 17th century under the Ottoman reign of Sultan Mehmed IV, the structure was commissioned by Ahmed Al-Saqqa, a prominent merchant of that era. In 1948, during the Nakba, it suffered damage from a shell but underwent subsequent restoration. It exemplifies the architectural style of the traditional Islamic Mumluk period, featuring characteristic elements such as an L-shaped entrance, a courtyard, an iwan, a cross-vault ceiling, wall storage, and ornamental detailing. The house used to host the Zakher Association for Developing Women Capacity since January 2015.

properties.Narratives: Gaza's Symbolic Monument Destroyed
properties.Description: A memorial built on the grave of an unidentified Palestinian soldier in the center of Gaza City, in the garden opposite the Palestinian Legislative Council building, was erected in 1957. It was destroyed by the Israeli Defense Forces in 1967, and the Palestinian Authority rebuilt it anew, with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat unveiling it in 2000. It holds symbolic importance for many residents of the Gaza Strip, with numerous national activities, events, and protest tents typically being held nearby.

properties.Narratives: Disruption of Life in Omar Al-Mukhtar Street
properties.Description: Omar al-Mukhtar Road was once the bustling high street of Gaza City, lined with an array of shops and hotels, as well as prominent landmarks such as the main mosques, the city hall, and the public library. Now both the street and the surrounding district have become a landscape of debris that will take years to restore.

properties.Narratives: Wadi Gaza Transforming into an Evacuation Line
properties.Description: Gaza valley extends for approximately 19 kilometers, with 8 kilometers of it located within the sector, and the rest within the settlements surrounding Gaza. It forms a line that divides Gaza into northern and southern parts and is considered one of the most densely populated areas of the sector. Historically, the banks of the lower valley in Gaza have attracted a number of ancient civilizations, leaving behind historical remains at approximately 15 sites. This has led many scholars to refer to the area as the "Gaza Valley Civilization" or the "Gaza Valley Group." Since October 7th, the occupation authorities demanded that over a million Palestinians leave the north and relocate to the southern part of the sector, turning the valley into a site of displacement for the Gazans.

properties.Narratives: Creating Life out of Nothing in Jabalia Refugee Camp
properties.Description: Ten months into the ongoing war and amid the huge destruction in Jabalia Camp, people show tremendous acts of resistance. Footage shows opening of makeshift shops, reclaiming open spaces, and cleaning the neighborhood from the dust and rubble.
properties.quotes: "This is Jabalia Camp ten months after the killing and destruction. From the beginning, I was amazed by the details I saw... how people create life from nothing, while I couldn't find the motivation to lift my phone to document a scene that surprised me. I wondered how they found hope amidst this ruin, how they defied themselves to keep going! Today, ten months after the killing and destruction, and after we in northern Gaza experienced all the violence of the this occupation, I created this incredible piece that you wouldn't believe comes from northern Gaza. This is Jabalia Camp, my birthplace, and with all pride, if you see a scene that impresses you and makes life seem normal, stop the video and zoom to the background to see the horrors. And if you don't find them, read the eyes and faces of the people. I am amazed by this creation; I am amazed by the people of life. I paused a lot before adding music because I didn't have the options to express how I felt. I don't know if hope is a blessing or a curse in this situation. What I am sure of is that we Palestinians suffer from the illness of hope. In the end, I will not stop documenting my life during this stage, even if all I have is my phone for documentation. " - Khaled Tuaima, Filmmaker SOURCE

properties.Narratives: A Gazan Farmer Reviving Agriculture amid Food Scarcity
properties.Description: Youssef Abu Rabie, a 24-year-old Agricultural Engineering graduate, is attempting to revive his family's land north of the Gaza Strip in Beit Lahia, as part of efforts to address food shortages in the enclave. He launched an initiative called 'Thamra Project' with a 21-year-old psychology student and photographer Leena Almadhoun. With roots deeply embedded in the land and communities of Gaza, Thamra strives to address food insecurity and promote resilience through sustainable agricultural practices and community-driven initiatives. The initiative planted 55,000 seedlings to support 100 families in north Gaza.
properties.Check_Fo_1: Check the video of Youssef speaking about his project here.
properties.Quote_1: "We were living through the most difficult kind of famine. The basic necessities that we could live on, such as flour, some vegetables, fruits or meat, were not available. This is when the idea of going back to farming came. My brother, who is also an engineer, and my father who supported us, wanted to go back to farming and return to our land, no matter the circumstances. Despite the difficult circumstances, the bombing and direct targeting in this place or in other agricultural lands, we insisted on staying, farming and producing." - Youssef Abu Rabie, Agricultural Engineering graduate

properties.description: Ahmad Abu Amsha, 42, a music teacher who had to flee Beit Hanun in the northern Gaza Strip, entertains children at the beach near a camp for displaced Palestinians in Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip where he took refuge with his family.
